doc_screened_files.reason: Highest priority because the bug is labeled `F-typeck-writeback` and `F-tainted-typeck-results`; this file is where body type-checking results are finalized and marked tainted so later MIR/codegen stages do not ICE after earlier errors like `E0666`/`E0562`.

The panic happens while building MIR for `f::{closure#0}` in `expr_into_dest`; this module owns the expression-lowering pipeline that consumes typeck results and drives the path that reaches the missing `as_place` guard.

The failing item is a closure body, and this file type-checks closure/coroutine expressions by deriving their expected signatures from context, which is central to handling `|_| p` under the invalid `impl Fn(impl T)` signature.

The reproducer captures `p` from the outer scope, and this file performs closure upvar analysis, capture-kind inference, and deferred closure-call bookkeeping that feed the closure body state used later by MIR building.

The query stack reaches `type_of_opaque`, and this file is responsible for finding and validating hidden types for opaque `impl Trait` items; the reproducer's outer `impl Fn(...)` return type makes this a likely contributor.

`type_of` is also on the query stack, and this is the main entry point that dispatches opaque-type hidden-type computation; any tainted or malformed type-of result here can cascade into later MIR building.

The file docs explicitly call out closure and opaque-type type-test conversion bugs as a source of wrong subjects/regions; that matches the query path through `mir_borrowck`/`type_of_opaque` for this nested-impl-Trait closure case.
This is the top-level MIR builder that orchestrates lowering the closure body before the crash site is reached, so it is the broader owner of the failing expression-lowering path.

Body type checking for the closure and its surrounding function flows through this file, so it is a plausible place where invalid signature information from the nested `impl Trait` can leave downstream consumers in an unsafe state.

Nested opaque types and late-bound capture handling are explicitly called out here; the invalid `impl Fn(impl T)` syntax combines binder/opaque handling with closure capture, making this a strong upstream candidate.
